facts.heading: Anxiety started in September
facts.content: Hannah has been anxious all the time and it got worse in September.
facts.evidence: I think I'm just anxious all the time and it got worse in September.

facts.heading: Work change caused anxiety
facts.content: Hannah's deputy head left, and she was asked to step up.
facts.evidence: when our deputy left.

facts.heading: Fear of incompetence
facts.content: Hannah keeps thinking someone will notice she has no idea what she is doing.
facts.evidence: I keep thinking they picked the wrong person, and that sooner or later someone will notice I have no idea what I'm doing.

facts.heading: Nighttime rehearsal of thoughts
facts.content: Hannah rehearses possible questions and what she would say in her head on Sunday evenings.
facts.evidence: Mostly Sunday evenings, my chest goes tight and I start rehearsing Monday's staff meeting in my head.

facts.heading: Fear of being judged
facts.content: Hannah imagines people thinking she is out of her depth.
facts.evidence: That I'm out of my depth.

facts.heading: Fear of being replaced
facts.content: Hannah imagines people thinking she was given the job to someone less capable.
facts.evidence: That they gave the job to a nice earful teacher who can't actually read.

facts.heading: Fear of appearing stupid
facts.content: Hannah was afraid Mr. Hargraves would think she was stupid regarding an email.
facts.evidence: I was afraid Mr. Hargraves, the chair of governors, would think that I was stupid.

facts.heading: Governor's reaction
facts.content: Mr. Hargraves told Hannah he was delighted in September.
facts.evidence: He told me in September he was delighted.

facts.heading: Feeling of deception
facts.content: Hannah feels like she is lying to Mr. Hargraves about her capability.
facts.evidence: I feel like I'm lying to him.

facts.heading: Identity comparison to mother
facts.content: Hannah feels like a child wearing her mother's coat.
facts.evidence: Most days I feel like a child wearing her mother's coat.

facts.heading: Mother's career history
facts.content: Hannah's mother was a headteacher for 20 years.
facts.evidence: She was a headteacher for 20 years.

facts.heading: Mother's legacy
facts.content: A library in the village is named after Hannah's mother.
facts.evidence: they have named a library after her.

facts.heading: Comparison to current role
facts.content: Hannah compares her deputy's job to her mother's position.
facts.evidence: A deputy's job, but yes, I can't help comparing.

facts.heading: Mother's supportive comments
facts.content: Hannah's mother says Hannah has always worried too much and should stop being silly.
facts.evidence: She says I've always worried too much and I should stop being silly.

facts.heading: Minimizing distress
facts.content: Hannah does not tell her mother how bad things are because it makes her feel like she is making a fuss.
facts.evidence: It makes me feel like I'm making a fuss, so I don't tell her how bad it is.

facts.heading: Waking late due to to-do list
facts.content: Hannah is awake at 4 every morning going through a to-do list. The list includes timetable changes, offset prep, a parent complaint, and a child she is worried about.
facts.evidence: I'm awake at 4 every morning. I fall asleep fine. Then I'm awake at 4 going through the to-do list. Everything. Timetable changes, the offset prep, a parent complaint, a child I'm worried about. It goes round and round.

facts.heading: Increased coffee consumption
facts.content: Hannah drinks a lot of coffee to get through the day since the second week of term. She feels this does not help.
facts.evidence: Since about the second week of term, I drink a lot of coffee to get through a day which I know doesn't help.

facts.heading: Physical symptoms during afternoons
facts.content: During the afternoons, Hannah notices her heart speeds up and her hands shake.
facts.evidence: My heart goes fast. My hands are a bit shaky.

facts.heading: Hiding physical symptoms
facts.content: Hannah had to leave a meeting to splash her face with water last Thursday. She did not think anyone noticed.
facts.evidence: Last Thursday, I had to leave a meeting to splash my face with water. I don't think so. I said I was fetching a document.

facts.heading: Exhaustion from pretending
facts.content: Hannah feels exhausted by the end of every day due to pretending.
facts.evidence: I am exhausted by the end of every day. Just from pretending.

facts.heading: Partner's advice reaction
facts.content: Hannah feels guilty and a bit alone when her partner Ben suggests she should just enjoy things.
facts.evidence: Guilty and a bit alone. He means well. He's an engineer. He thinks if something's a problem, you fix it. You can't just fix this. No, I wish it were that simple.

facts.heading: Loss of school friends
facts.content: Hannah does not have friends at school to talk to anymore. She used to eat lunch with others.
facts.evidence: Not anymore, not really. I used to eat lunch in the year for a quarter with the others.

facts.heading: Lost company with promotion
facts.content: Hannah lost some company along with her promotion. She had not thought of it that way before.
facts.evidence: So you lost some company along with the promotion? Yes, I hadn't thought of it like that.

facts.heading: Missing children and daily life
facts.content: Hannah misses the children most. She misses the daily experience of a child getting something for the first time.
facts.evidence: The children mostly. The daily bit where a child gets something for the first time.

facts.heading: Work life is spreadsheets
facts.content: Hannah's days are now filled with spreadsheets.
facts.evidence: No, my days are spreadsheets.

facts.heading: Wanted the promotion
facts.content: Hannah thought she wanted the promotion. She said yes because she could not say no to her.
facts.evidence: I thought I did. I said yes in the room because I couldn't say no to her.

facts.heading: Cried after accepting promotion
facts.content: Hannah went home and cried after accepting the promotion. The tears were about fear and never getting back.
facts.evidence: Then I went home and cried. What were the tears about? Fear, I think. And that I would never get to go back.

facts.heading: Last time feeling relaxed
facts.content: Hannah felt properly relaxed during the summer holidays. She went walking in the lakes and did not think about school for ten days.
facts.evidence: These summer holidays. We went walking in the lakes and I didn't think about school once for ten days.

facts.heading: Wreck before term started
facts.content: The week before term started, Hannah was a wreck again. She could not eat on Sunday.
facts.evidence: The week before term, I was a wreck again. I couldn't eat on the Sunday.

facts.heading: Tried writing down good things
facts.content: Hannah tried writing down things that went well each evening. This practice lasted for about two weeks.
facts.evidence: I started writing down what went well each evening. Small things, a true laughing, a good email. It held for about two weeks, and then I stopped because I felt silly.

facts.heading: Wants to do job without fraud
facts.content: Hannah wants to do her job without feeling like a fraud. This involves not rehearsing in meetings and sending only one email.
facts.evidence: I would like to do the job without feeling like a fraud. Walking into a meeting and not rehearsing at first. Sending an email once.

facts.heading: Wants calm evenings
facts.content: Hannah wants to be able to sit on the sofa in the evening without stomach knots.
facts.evidence: Being able to sit on the sofa in the evening without my stomach in knots.

facts.heading: Feels lightful after goals
facts.content: Hannah felt lightful and lighter after stating her goals out loud. She also felt a bit tearful.
facts.evidence: Lightful. Lighter. A bit tearful actually.

facts.heading: First time sharing bad news
facts.content: This is the first time Hannah has told anyone how bad her situation is. She has not told Ben about the 4am issue.
facts.evidence: It's the first time I have told anyone how bad it is. Not even Ben knows how about the 4am.

facts.heading: Worried about telling Ben
facts.content: Hannah feels scared about telling Ben how bad things are. She worries he would be hurt that she did not say sooner.
facts.evidence: Scary. He would probably be hurt that I didn't say sooner.

facts.heading: Plan to tell Ben this week
facts.content: Hannah might try telling Ben this week. She needs a quiet moment, not on a Sunday evening, to do this.
facts.evidence: I might try this week. If I choose a quiet moment, not on a Sunday evening.

facts.heading: Suggests Saturday morning time
facts.content: Hannah suggested a Saturday morning over breakfast as a time to tell Ben. She noted he is usually in a good mood then.
facts.evidence: Saturday morning, perhaps? Yeah, over breakfast. He is always in a good mood then.

facts.heading: Wants to try notebook again
facts.content: Hannah considered trying the evening notebook again for a week, even just one line.
facts.evidence: Would you try the evening notebook again, just for a week? Even one line? I could.
